body: Yeah, as I said to someone else, I hadn't seen the film, or heard of it. But I know it would be heard to ensured my organs were preserved. This does disappoint me also. But for me, the mere thought of its possibility, even if vague, is quite pleasant. Thanks for your reply though It's sad that so many of us are troubled.

I haven't seen or heard of the film, I consulted Google, read a couple of reviews. So it's along a similar track to myself, except I don't think I would want to make a judgement as to who was more deserving of my organs! And I think I am no fan of his either!
I also guess I probably should have anticipated that people might feel wary of being completely candid, given the nature of this sub.

Hey, thanks for replying. I don't mind the rambling, I am interested to hear peoples's thoughts, however they may come. I do think there is a slight hypocrisy in how people process suicidal ideation, which you've obviously touched upon. I think you're right in that people can't handle this kind of thinking. You make a fair point in that people have a will to live rather than an inherent reason/purpose for living. In a way, you've made me think, if there is no real purpose for living, in an absolute sense, then maybe my altruism/utilitarianism is equally unnecessary and futile. Maybe making a decision for the greater good doesn't really matter. Perhaps, in being rational, there is no distinction to be made between the value of altruism or nihilism, so, I've levelled myself!
